_comment: Each source is either (a) verified by web search this session, (b) computed directly from the repository's own files, or (c) marked unverified. Citation IDs used in the transcript as [S#].

sources.title: WCAG 2.x relative-luminance contrast ratios for every CSS custom-property pair in :root, light and dark
sources.note: Computed directly with the sRGB->linear->relative-luminance formula, not estimated. Working: /scratchpad/contrast.py this session. Confirms the author's own inline claims (accent/bg 6.06:1 light, 8.27:1 dark) exactly, and adds pairs the comments don't address (faint/bg: 4.87:1 light, 4.62:1 dark -- the dark figure is 0.12 above the 4.5:1 AA floor for small text, the thinnest margin on the page).

sources.title: WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), Level AA -- 24x24 CSS px; WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), Level AAA -- 44x44 CSS px
sources.note: Confirms the page's own CSS comments (lines 159-165, 204-210) cite the correct numbers for the correct levels: 2.25rem=36px clears 24px (AA) but not 44px (AAA) on desktop; the phone override to 2.75rem=44px clears AAA.

sources.title: B.J. Fogg, 'A Behavior Model for Persuasive Design', Persuasive 2009 (B=MAT); Fogg, Tiny Habits, 2019 (B=MAP, trigger renamed prompt)
sources.note: Behaviour requires motivation, ability and a prompt at the same moment. Grounds the panel's Fogg seat.

sources.title: Jakob Nielsen, 'How Users Read on the Web', Alertbox, Oct 1997; 'F-Shaped Pattern for Reading Web Content', Alertbox, 17 Apr 2006 (eyetracking, n=232)
sources.note: Users scan rather than read; attention concentrates top-left, decaying rightward and downward -- the empirical basis for Nielsen's reads of row order in the transcript.

sources.title: Dieter Rams, ten principles for good design (Vitsoe, from a 1976 talk)
sources.note: Principle 10, 'as little design as possible / less, but better', and principle 4, 'makes a product understandable', both cited directly.

sources.title: Edward Tufte, The Visual Display of Quantitative Information (1983) -- data-ink ratio, chartjunk, graphical integrity/lie factor
sources.note: Lie factor = (size of effect shown)/(size of effect in data); 1.0 is honest. Applied to the .gauge element's proportions.

sources.title: Loomio four-position model: agree / disagree / abstain / block, with abstain explicitly meaning 'this doesn't affect me and I'm happy with whatever the group decides'
sources.note: A real four-position deliberation tool whose 'abstain' is a genuinely different, intentionally weak-affirmative signal from Newspeak's toleration -- a direct comparator for the toleration question. Loomio also visualises disagreement as a pie chart staff describe as something 'you must pay attention to.'

sources.title: Pluralistic ignorance (social psychology): individuals privately dissent but believe others don't, so public silence is read as agreement; Geiger & Swim suggest correcting it by showing people that others share their concern
sources.note: Grounds the panel's discussion of why a bare 'not yet answered: X, Y, Z' list may not be the most effective nudge, and why a base-rate framing (see R7 in recommendations) could outperform it. General mechanism cited; the specific Geiger & Swim intervention-design claim is noted as plausible but not independently verified against the primary paper this session -- marked unverified at that level of detail.

sources.title: Gerber & Rogers, 'Descriptive Social Norms and Motivation to Vote: Everybody's Voting and So Should You', Journal of Politics 71(1), 2009, pp.178-191
sources.note: Field experiment, NJ 2005 / CA 2006 gubernatorial elections: a high-turnout descriptive-norm script raised self-reported voting probability ~7pp versus a low-turnout script, concentrated among infrequent voters. Directly relevant to whether a 'most members have already voted' framing would help or backfire on a 14-person roll where the true norm may be low participation (in which case the honest descriptive norm cuts the other way -- flagged as a tension in the transcript, not a clean win).

sources.title: GOV.UK Service Manual / content style guide: 'open up, don't dumb down'; active voice; 'must' for legal obligation; front-loaded sentences
sources.note: A real, large-scale, tested precedent for rendering legal/procedural obligation in plain language without losing precision -- the closest existing institutional analogue to this page's problem. Cited by Orwell and Nielsen's seats as an available standard to hold the page's sentences against.

sources.title: George Orwell, 'Politics and the English Language', Horizon, 1946 -- six rules, incl. 'never use the passive where you can use the active' and 'never use a long word where a short one will do'
sources.note: Applied directly to specific sentences in docs/index.html in the transcript (e.g. the Carries-if line, the toleration paragraph).

sources.title: Christopher Alexander, The Timeless Way of Building (1979), 'the quality without a name'; A Pattern Language (1977)
sources.note: Used to ask whether the page's correctness produces 'life' or only produces correctness -- a qualitative, admittedly harder-to-falsify register, flagged as such whenever Alexander's seat makes a claim that resists the contrast-ratio treatment the rest of the panel uses.

sources.title: Gestalt grouping principles (proximity, similarity, figure-ground) as standard UI-design vocabulary
sources.note: General textbook material, not attributed to a single paper; used descriptively for the row/tag/vote-block layout discussion.

sources.title: Fitts's Law, Paul Fitts, 1954; MT = a + b*log2(2D/W)
sources.note: Target acquisition time grows with distance, shrinks with width -- the formal version of the reasoning already in the page's own CSS comments about the 44px CTA.

sources.title: Matthew Butterick, Practical Typography -- tabular vs. proportional figures; many proportional fonts already support font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums without needing a full monospace face
sources.note: Relevant to a minor, low-priority finding: tabular-nums applied to .rem/.abs, which already sit in a monospace stack, is redundant (harmless, but a sign the rule may have been copied rather than reasoned about for this specific case).

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group, 'Progress Indicators Make a Slow System Less Insufferable'
sources.note: Guidance is aimed at wait-states (loading), not status gauges -- cited to note the .gauge element is doing a different job (showing a static ratio, not elapsing time) than NN/g's progress-indicator guidance covers, so that guidance is not directly transferable and is not cited as if it endorses the gauge.
